answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, any migration risk from switching primary vendors (memory_c2) could jeopardize delivery just when there's no slack to absorb disruption. Verifying memory_c4 confirms that benchmarking-driven renegotiation with the incumbent has previously recovered real margin on both price and terms without altering service scope or continuity, and memory_c6 shows the incumbent has flexed on pricing before under longer commitments. Given finance's 18% cost mandate must be met without increasing delivery risk, negotiating harder with the known, stable incumbent is the lowest-risk lever this cycle. Switching vendors remains attractive on paper but the onboarding/integration risk (even if it went smoothly once per memory_c2) is not something to gamble on with no volume buffer. Second-sourcing and deferral are deprioritized this cycle since they don't directly address the imminent contract expiration or the immediate margin mandate.
